cases.excerpt: 1,602 incident invasive prostate cancers were obtained from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results registry.

effect_size.excerpt: We selected a priori potential confounders, including known or suspected risk factors for prostate cancer or prostate cancer diagnosis. headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test was not performed because fewer than 10 studies were available. With a small number of studies, the test generally has insufficient power to reliably detect funnel plot asymmetry.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 3 studies yielded an effect size of 0.69 (95% CI: 0.42–1.13), indicating no statistically significant association between garlic and prostate cancer\aggressive. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 85.03%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
